judged_text: The EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, yet updateCalendarAttendees must modify the organizer's calendar event. When the caller is an attendee or team admin — the classes the permission gate at lines 54-56 explicitly admits — their credential list contains no match for the organizer's destinationCalendar credentialId, so the calendar attendee update silently no-ops and Google/Outlook attendee lists permanently diverge from the booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update path builds `EventManager` using the requesting user (`const { user } = ctx;` then `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`) and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The permission gate explicitly allows non-organizers (attendees via `isAttendee`, and team admins/owners via `isTeamAdminOrOwner`), so callers other than `booking.userId` can reach this code. The diff shows organizer/calendar ownership data is available (`booking.user` is included with `credentials` and `destinationCalendar`), but it is not used for the calendar update. This makes it very likely that updates to the organizer’s destination calendar will fail/no-op when invoked by an attendee/admin without the organizer’s calendar credentials.
